summary: Ground cab lookout on Picuris Peak in the Carson National Forest, Taos County, NM; built about 1928-1932, regularly staffed through 1990, NHLR-registered 2016.

facts.design: Ground cab of the L-4 type; sources give different sizes

staffing.status: occasional use only, in times of extreme fire danger

events.note: Taos News gives 1932; the 2020 chapter report says constructed between 1928 and 1932; West Lookouts says c.1930 give or take a couple of years
Eli Romero says he began staffing the tower in 1958 and worked there about three decades
Thematic National Register review of Southwest Region lookouts (1988) recommended it be found ineligible for the National Register
Regularly staffed through 1990; used only occasionally since, in times of extreme fire danger

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 2020 chapter report gives 1928 to 1932; Taos News gives 1932; West Lookouts gives about 1930. The event keeps 1932 as its year and the story gives the range.
NHLR lists 10,752 ft; the Taos News says 10,801 ft. The story gives both.
West Lookouts describes a 12 by 12 ft ground cabin; the Taos News describes L-4 cabins as 14 by 14 ft in design. The story says the sizes differ.

notes_for_editor: Access not established: no source read says whether the cabin is open to visitors, so no visit or climbing advice is given. NHLR links a 2001 Albuquerque Journal article that returned 404 and was not used. The Taos News article is undated in my copy. Its first fetch returned 429 and a retry succeeded. The staffing as_of is undated because the NHLR description carries no date. No photos added (no image URLs read).
